idea-plugin.name: Second-Order SQLi Field Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Flags a SQL sink concatenating a @Entity field's getter/direct read, when that SAME field is ALSO confirmed, elsewhere in the project, to be written from unsanitized HTTP input -- CWE-89, the second-order form: the tainted value passes through persistent storage (a real database) between the write and the read, invisible to any single-method or single-call-chain taint check.

Built on a real FIELD-SENSITIVE, two-phase, whole-project points-to analysis -- the write site and the read site can live in completely unrelated classes with no call-graph relationship whatsoever; the field NAME itself is the only thing connecting them, exactly the shape documented as the real blind spot of simple pattern-matching SAST tools ("SAST tools excel at direct input-to-query flows but struggle when malicious data is stored and later used in a different execution context").

Stated honestly: Checkmarx and Fortify (real, confirmed enterprise SAST tools) model this exact pattern -- neither is free, an inline IDE plugin, or Community-Edition-compatible. No dedicated Marketplace plugin found.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

localInspection.displayName: Persisted field written from tainted input reaches a SQL sink
